findings.title: Recheck time-based authority before committing a tool result
evidence: packages/core/src/agents-tools.ts:219 â€” result transaction checks assertToolTransaction at entry, then awaits quota read and allocation/call updates through line 257 without a closing time/abort fence.
packages/core/src/agents-tools.ts:25 â€” Foundation grant/lease validation occurs before subsequent awaited profile/allocation reads.
packages/core/src/foundation-grants.ts:80 â€” grant expiry is checked against state.now only during validateGrant.
packages/core/src/agents-tools.ts:259 â€” next authority check executes after transaction commit; catch at line 271 subsequently changes state to unknown.
packages/core/src/agents-tools-lifecycle.ts:163 â€” owner detail validates succeeded/failed observations and exposes their result at line 207 during the post-commit interval.
findings.scenario: A valid tool completes just before the immutable allocation deadline, task lease/grant expiry or AbortController deadline. Advance fixture time or abort while the publication transaction awaits its quota select or final update. The entry check passed, so a succeeded observation commits after authority expired. The post-commit assertToolActive can eventually change its state to unknown, but an owner reader can already observe the committed result; a process interruption in that interval leaves it retained as succeeded.
findings.refutation: The serialized control_lock prevents concurrent control-plane cancellation/epoch/profile writes from interleaving inside this transaction, and executeAgent has later fences before task success. Those safeguards narrow the impact: this is time/abort expiry and tool-result publication, not a demonstrated cross-task escape or final artifact export bypass. Wall-clock expiry and signal abort still occur while the transaction awaits, and the post-commit fence cannot roll back an already published result.
findings.suggestion: Capture/validate the exact lease, grant and allocation deadlines and signal again at the closing transaction boundary after relevant awaits, throwing inside the transaction to roll back result/quota publication. Add a deterministic clock/abort edge regression at that boundary.
findings.verification: Static source interleaving; deterministic executable regression requested from the core implementation worker. No production changes by reviewer.
findings.remediation_status: Resolved: frozen source delta verified and actual-executor transaction-boundary regression passed.

remediation_review.refutation: A final assertion that itself awaits could otherwise repeat the original issue. This implementation captures exact grant and run and performs clock/signal checks synchronously after its final await. The existing serialized control lock excludes concurrent logical authority mutations until transaction completion. Asynchronous database COMMIT is an unavoidable transaction boundary; no additional application I/O is interposed after this guard.
